claim: It reacts to unhandled exceptions that Laravel reports, through a reportable hook on the exception handler.
A crash queues an email to you (delivery depends on the queue and mail setup).
The email goes to MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS unless a developer sets EXCEPTION_REPORT_RECIPIENT, and there is no admin setting for it.
There is no page of errors and no way to mark one resolved (no Filament classes, no admin surface in the manifest).

Each exception is also saved as a small database record (class, scrubbed message, job, URL, time) that the admin does not show, with persistence on by default. A daily scheduled prune, which runs only if the server's scheduler is running, deletes records older than 30 days by default, and a retention of 0 days keeps them forever
If a developer enables it, the same report goes to a webhook at an approved HTTPS host, off by default.
By default identical errors send one email per 15 minutes and no more than ten go out per hour in total.
Anything held back is still saved but not emailed (the record is written before the throttle, and the digest is off by default).
Each email names the error, the file and line, and the environment.
It names the page or command by its route name, action or command name, not the visited address, which is redacted.
The subject line carries the app name, the error type and that page or command.
